newsitem.title: UK: Air Canada takes delivery of first A319.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada takes delivery of first A319.

text.p: Air Canada has taken delivery of the first of 35 Airbus Industrie A319 aircraft, the airline said on Thursday.

Deliveries of the remaining 34 planes -- configured to provide 112 seats -- will continue at a rate of approximately two a month, until all have been received by June 1998, the company said in a statement.
The A319 will eventually replace the airline's Douglas DC-9 aircraft.
Air Canada president and chief executive officer, Lamar Durrett, added: "The A319 nicely fits our niche markets between those served by the 50 seat Canadair jet and the 132 seat A320."

"Just as our open skies routes between Canada and the U.S. are growing and developing, the A319 is making its entrance.... It's a perfect complement to the fleet and represents a distinct cost advantage over our competitors," he said.
The delivery of all 35 A319 aircraft will provide Air Canada with the largest North American Airbus fleet.
It currently operates 32 A320s with options for a further six and three long-haul A340s with five on order and options for three, the statement said.
